When both `image_path` and `artifact_id` are present in the payload, `AgenticHILToolService.flash_firmware` rejects the call.

Specifically, in `src/agentic_hil/tools.py` (lines 280–283):

```python
image_path = payload.get("image_path")
artifact_id = payload.get("artifact_id")
if bool(image_path) == bool(artifact_id):
    return tool_error("flash_firmware", "invalid_argument", "Provide exactly one of image_path or artifact_id.")
```

Since `bool(image_path) == bool(artifact_id)` is true both when both are absent and when both are present, supplying both fields causes it to short-circuit with an `invalid_argument` error ("Provide exactly one of image_path or artifact_id.") before any permission checks beyond `allow_flash`, artifact validation, staging, or the actual backend `flash_firmware` call occur. This matches the contract schema in `src/agentic_hil/contracts.py` (the `flash_firmware` tool definition uses `one_of=[{"required": ["image_path"]}, {"required": ["artifact_id"]}]`), enforcing mutual exclusivity of the two fields.
